Subject: Post-demo: fit signal & compression sensitivity — headroom and next steps

Hi Emma / Paul —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and helpful signal on the workload shape. Quick recap from our side and recommended next steps so we land on an actionable POC.

What we heard (short):
- Primary goal: 1) extract structured assay metadata from freeform lab notes; 2) keep generation consistency for short prompts (~40–120 tokens).
- Target quality bar: production-like accuracy on your golden set (we heard ~92% acceptance on your QA rubric).
- Throughput expectation: bursts up to ~250 qps for batch calls during peak ingest.

Model-fit & compression summary (initial recommendations):
- Candidate families: Llama-2-13B-chat (instruction-tuned), Mistral-instruct-7B, Falcon-40B-instruct (if you need larger-context reasoning).
- Quantization options to try: AWQ-8bit on Llama-2-13B (best throughput/quality balance for short instruction patterns), GPTQ-4bit on Mistral (aggressive cost reduction, watch prompt-sensitive regressions), FP8 experimental runs on Falcon-40B for high-throughput low-latency (higher memory but good perf on our infra).
- Quick heuristic: expect ~0.5–2% absolute drop on model-stability QA for AWQ depending on prompt fragility; GPTQ-4bit can show larger deltas on instruction-following prompts. We’ll quantify with your golden set.

Attachments / links: attached a first-pass prompt set you dropped in the call (sierra_promptset_v1.csv) and a short benchmarking snapshot (rw_benchmarks_summary.pdf). Full head-to-head scripts and dashboards are in the Drive link below.

Proposed next steps (we can start immediately):
1) Redwood runs a 5k-example eval (your golden set + adversarial slices) across 3 variants (L2-13B AWQ-8, Mistral GPTQ-4, Falcon FP8) — deliverable: per-prompt pass/fail, latency/tokens/sec, and a small “regression heatmap”. (ETA: 3 business days after we get confirm + access to the test set)
2) Quick canary: host the winning variant in a non-prod Dedicated pool for a week (we’ll configure autoscaling & monitor SLOs).
3) Reconvene and decide on pilot commit / pricing.

Can you confirm: 1) we have permission to run the eval on the attached prompt set (or point us to an updated golden set), and 2) whether you want us to include Falcon runs in the first pass (it’s heavier but useful for edge cases)?

I can book a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to align on access and timeline.

Thanks —
Sergio

Thanks for the permission, Emma — quick technical note from the SE side so expectations are aligned before we run the head-to-head.

1) Expected quality ranges (ballpark, will verify on your golden set):
   - Llama-2-13B (AWQ-8bit): QA score delta typically ~ -0.3% to -1.2% absolute on short instruction/slot-fill tasks; worst-case on brittle prompts we’ve seen up to -1.8%.
   - Mistral-7B (GPTQ-4bit): cost-friendly, but instruction-following can degrade more — expect ~ -1.0% to -2.5% depending on prompt complexity.
   - Falcon-40B (FP8 trials): often retains quality well on long-context reasoning but requires more infra; delta usually under -0.5% on our internal tests for similar tasks.

2) Latency / throughput (typical on Redwood Dedicated x4 A100-equivalent pool):
   - L2-13B AWQ-8: 8–12 ms per token p50; ~350–600 tokens/sec sustained depending on batching and prefix caching.
   - Mistral GPTQ-4: 6–10 ms per token p50; ~450–700 tokens/sec (smaller memory footprint helps concurrency).
   - Falcon FP8 (40B): 10–18 ms per token p50; lower tokens/sec but better for long context reasoning.

Hosted vs Dedicated: hosted gives quick onboarding and burstable capacity; Dedicated reduces tail variance and gives predictable SLOs (important if you have tight latency SLAs). For your 250 qps bursts, Dedicated is recommended for predictable performance unless you accept a wider latency SLA window.

3) Proposed eval plan (attached eval_plan_v1.md):
   - Step A: run the 5k golden set across the 3 variants and produce per-example diff + failure clusters.
   - Step B: run adversarial slice (200 edge cases) to stress instruction-following behavior.
   - Step C: produce a single-sheet recommendation mapping quality vs cost vs latency.

ETA: 3 business days after we get read access to the test bucket and a short API key with test usage enabled. Cost: we’ll absorb the first smoke runs; if you want Dedicated pilot we’ll propose a short-term pilot fee.

Happy to sync 2pm PT tomorrow; I’ll put a tentative hold.

—Marissa
